To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
L. plantarun L9 but not LA reduce TNF-α-induced E. coli translocation and IL8 production in C2-6 cells.
L. plantarun L9, but not L. acidophilis LA, reduces the TNF-α-induced bacterial translocation in a human intestinal epithelial cell line (Caco-2).
Lactobacilli can inhibit the translocation of E. coli across Caco- 2 monolayers, and that Lactobacterium plantarum L-9 can protect the monolayers from TNF-α- induced bacterial translocation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential of the Lactobacilli to inhibit bacterial translocation across the gut epithelial barrier.
the potential use of probiotic strains in the prevention of bacterial translocation in inflammatory bowel disease and other conditions where gut permeability is compromised.
the protective role of Lactobacterial species against the TNF-α-induced non-pathogenic Es. coli translocation across intestinal epithelium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
L. plantarums L9 is a good candidate to reduce bacterial translocation across the intestinal mucosa, and therefore could be a potential probiotic in counteracting bacterial infections.
L. plantarium L9 is a good probiotic candidate for preventing bacterial translocation across the intestinal barrier.
L. plantarums L9 is a potential candidate for the treatment of bacterial translocation in the gut.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

L. plantarun L9 has the potential to protect Caco-2 epithelial cells from an acute inflammatory challenge and therefore could be a good potential prophylaxis against bacterial translocation in patients with sepsis.
L. plantarun L9 has the potential to prevent TNF- α induced bacterial translocation across Cacao-2 cells.
L. plantarium L9 has the potential to prevent bacterial translocation across enterocyte monolayers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of Lactobalilli strains in the treatment of patients at risk of bacterial translocation is not a straightforward process.
L. plantarums L9 is a good candidate for the development of probiotics to be used as a preventive strategy to counteract bacterial translocation in critically ill patients.
probiotics can reduce TNF-α-induced transcellular bacterial uptake in a model of enterocytes.
